From 2b7eb2c5dc72f0fc954ac4aa155f9e285e937f7c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Sakari Ailus <sakari.ailus@linux.intel.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 15:10:54 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] staging: media: atomisp: Disallow all private IOCTLs

Disallow all private IOCTLs. These aren't quite as safe as one could
assume of IOCTL handlers; disable them for now. Instead of removing the
code, return in the beginning of the function if cmd is non-zero in order
to keep static checkers happy.

Reported-by: Soufiane Dani <soufianeda@tutanota.com>
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-staging/20260210-atomisp-fix-v1-1-024429cbff31@tutanota.com/
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: a49d25364dfb ("staging/atomisp: Add support for the Intel IPU v2")
Fixes: ad85094b293e ("Revert "media: staging: atomisp: Remove driver"")
Signed-off-by: Sakari Ailus <sakari.ailus@linux.intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab+huawei@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/staging/media/atomisp/pci/atomisp_ioctl.c b/drivers/staging/media/atomisp/pci/atomisp_ioctl.c
index a7f22de1c889..50366bf10f32 100644
--- a/drivers/staging/media/atomisp/pci/atomisp_ioctl.c
+++ b/drivers/staging/media/atomisp/pci/atomisp_ioctl.c
@@ -1356,6 +1356,10 @@ static int atomisp_s_parm(struct file *file, void *fh,
 static long atomisp_vidioc_default(struct file *file, void *fh,
 				   bool valid_prio, unsigned int cmd, void *arg)
 {
+	/* Disable all private IOCTLs for now! */
+	if (cmd)
+		return -EINVAL;
+
 	struct video_device *vdev = video_devdata(file);
 	struct atomisp_sub_device *asd = atomisp_to_video_pipe(vdev)->asd;
 	int err;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### 1. Modifications in Each File

**File:** `drivers/staging/media/atomisp/pci/atomisp_ioctl.c`

- **Change:** In the function `atomisp_vidioc_default()`, an early return of `-EINVAL` is added for any non-zero command value (`cmd`).  
  - Code added:  
    ```c
    /* Disable all private IOCTLs for now! */
    if (cmd)
        return -EINVAL;
    ```
  - This check is placed right before the existing code that handles the IOCTL, causing the function to reject all private IOCTLs (which have a non-zero `cmd`) immediately.

- **Effect:** Private IOCTLs (those with `cmd != 0`) are no longer processed; the function returns an error (`-EINVAL`) before reaching any potentially unsafe handler logic.

### 2. Relationships Between Modifications

- The single change in `atomisp_vidioc_default()` is the only modification in this patch.  
- The purpose is to disable all private IOCTLs entirely, as they are deemed unsafe. By returning early for any non-zero command, the function avoids executing any of the downstream handler code that could be vulnerable.  
- The patch intentionally preserves the existing code structure (rather than removing it) to avoid breaking static analysis tools or requiring major refactoring, while still preventing any actual execution of private IOCTLs.  
- This change addresses a reported security concern (reported by Soufiane Dani) and fixes potential issues introduced by commits `a49d25364dfb` and `ad85094b293e`.
